notes: SHAPE (8 bars, four-on-the-floor, crashes on hb:48, hb:50 and hb:67, the only snare on hb:70, the fill 57.22-57.94): one couplet per two bars, and the energy rises in three steps. Bars 12-13 (hb:48-55) are pure music: screenshot piles and footage hit on every beat (teens on 'sick of seventeen', then the dream essays on 'teenage dream'). Bars 14-17 (hb:56-71) are the voice collage: Amodei counting the doublings, then the 60 Minutes exchange, ducked 8 dB under the sung lines, with every spoken number or 'no one' landing on a beat. Bars 18-19 (hb:72-79) are pure music again: the GRPO drop over the inside of the data hall, the warnings pile and Gallup, and then the fill.

THE HERO: Epoch's dc-record-mw chart, 8 beats (hb:64-72). The records land on 8ths, so the 946 MW Colossus 2 record lands ON the hb:67 crash (sung 'myself'). The callout 'Colossus 2: 946 MW' slams on hb:67.5 and reads clean until hb:71.07, when the zoom-through dives into that very point and comes out inside xAI's Colossus data hall (the GRPO scene). No transition crosses the hero; its beat events are its own data landings, marks and kicks.

THE EQUATION: GRPO (equations.json, the portrait-stacked tex). Its three rows are chalked on beats hb:72 / 72.75 / 73.5, and it is whole on screen from ~hb:74.3 to hb:79.7 (2.6 s). Its terms are lit on the sung words: KL to the reference model on 'before', the group mean 1/G Σ on 'people', Â on 'liked'. The advantage formula (same paper, sec. 4.1.2) then slams under it on hb:77, so that 'liked me more' has its maths: your reward minus the group's mean.

THE EYE: one lead phrase per couplet, always the last thing highlighted. 'Nearly 3 in 4 Teens Have Used AI Companions' (lifted hb:51.25), then 'The Adolescence of Technology… Risks of Powerful AI' (hb:54.5-55), then "now it's every ~11 days" (hb:59), then 'Computer Science Has Lost 53,000 Majors' (hb:62), then the record and 'Colossus 2: 946 MW' with Amodei's 'No one' (hb:67-71), then 'OpenAI ignored employees who warned it wasn't doing enough about security' (hb:75), then Â and 'Americans Cool Toward AI' (hb:77-79).

LAYOUT (safe zone x 60-1014, y 250-1574; right rail x > 930, y 1000-1600 carries no text). Footage masks sit in the top band: centred circle or blob at y 300-780 in bars 12-13, then a circle top right (cx 800, cy 470, r 190) with the karaoke left of it (x 72-592) in bars 14-17. Piles and the chart card sit at y 760-1550. Stamps and beatfx paint use the top strip (y 140-250), the gap (y 700-870), the bottom strip (y 1590-1880) and the edges. GRPO card at y 390-770 with its label above, the advantage at y 860-1010, and the bottom pile at y 1080-1500.

LAYERING (EDL order, bottom to top): g-ch-cream, ch-paper, the shared paint layer, v-racks (bars 18-19), panels, piles, chart, karaoke, equations, own-layer stamps and the stroke. Footage or an image is in every frame: Sora 2, the protein binders, Amodei on CBS, the 60 Minutes circle, the Colossus racks, plus the screenshots and the chart. The transitions use the frames' own pixels.

AUDIO: two snippets, 3.46 s and 4.26 s, 0.21 s apart, so mix.py merges them into one duck of 8 dB from ~46.17 to ~54.34 (120 ms ramps). Both were re-transcribed with small.en on 11 Oct and agree with base.en. The 60 Minutes words were also checked against the CBS transcript page (16 Nov 2025: Cooper asks, Amodei answers). Speakers were checked on the picture (scene cuts plus frames): Amodei is on camera for the whole count; Cooper is on camera asking and Amodei answering. Nothing is spoken under the explicit word (44.88-45.22), and both no-song versions carry the two snippets.

MEANING: the count keeps its numbers. The leading ellipsis marks the trimmed 'It's like you have', and its context is 'this technology is on an exponential'. The count is NOT synced to the chart's data points, because the chart's values are Epoch's MW and his numbers are a generic doubling, and the two scenes are separated by a transition. The 60 Minutes answer is kept whole ('No one, no one. Honestly, no one.'); only Cooper's 'Like,' is trimmed. The data-centre chart shows Epoch's observed records only, no projections, under the graph's own title and source. Labels on equation cards are explanatory, not quotes. Older items: Hinton quits Google and the FLI Pause letter (2023), used as the early warnings 'before'. Everything else is 2024-2026.

SENSITIVITY: from the teen candidates (research/long/lyrics/sick-of-seventeen.json and screens.json lyric 'sick-of-seventeen') the plan uses the survey and safety headlines (Common Sense, Thorn, Education Week, UNICEF) and leaves out the teen-suicide lawsuit and the 'AI nudes' headlines.

TRANSITIONS (impact beats): 48 illuminate (verse, shared), 50 shatter (pile region), 52 fold, 54 page turn (essay region), 56 whip spin, 60 iris square (pile region), 64 paint wipe (cover), 67.75 iris ring (karaoke enterFx), 72 zoom-through, 73 paint wipe matte (pile enterFx), 76 shatter (pile region), 80 iris circle (refrain, shared). That is 12 transitions; every other item change is a beat-locked pile landing. Every beat also carries a beatfx paint effect and a camera move (four tracks), and most 8ths carry a marker, a push, a lift, a pencil mark or a lit karaoke word.

PERFORMANCE: chart + two karaoke + a panel ~0.3-0.4 s/frame; the shatters (12-14 clones) and the zoom-through ~0.5; the racks clip is full-frame 1080x1920 from a 1920x1080 source (prep crops 607x1080 and upscales: soft but it is background). Prep: python3 render/video/prep_clips.py <edl> extracts p-sora, p-protein, p-cbs, p-60 (frame-sized) and v-racks, and copies the screenshots.

RISKS TO CHECK ON THE FIRST STRIP: (1) the zoom-through focus [865, 1030] must sit on the 946 MW point (engine request 1); (2) the callout at dx -560 / dy -10 must not cross the step line; (3) pile-youth has three tall cards in 620 px (overlap up to 0.4); (4) the Common Sense push z 1.7 must keep the phrase inside 940 px; (5) the four-line count karaoke must clear the CBS circle at x 610; (6) the in-point 158.12 must not let the tail of 'have' through (move to 158.15 if it does).
